articles.title: Four beluga whales on way to Shedd from closed Canadian park: report
articles.description:
Four beluga whales from a shuttered aquatic park in Niagara Falls, Canada, were on their way to Shedd Aquarium Monday as part of an “unprecedented rescue effort,” according to Canadian media.

Two more whales were headed to SeaWorld in San Antonio Monday, according to The Canadian Press.

It’s the first phase of a plan to move up to 30 belugas over the next few weeks from Marineland to several American aquariums as well as to Oceanografic Valencia in Spain. Earlier this month, Shedd announced it could receive as many as 10 belugas from Marineland.

Shedd officials declined Monday to offer a timeline for when the whales would arrive at the aquarium or to confirm Canadian press reports that they were in fact on their way to Chicago.

“As reported, an initial rescue of the belugas at Marineland of Canada is under way. This is a complex rescue operation and experts are focused on the immediate safety and comfort of the animals involved. The group of accredited aquariums will share more details and updates as animals arrive safely to their new homes,” said Kayley Galassini, Shedd’s director of public relations.

The belugas headed to Shedd are named Sierra, Acadia, Osiris and Lillooet, The Canadian Press reported.

The future of the beluga whales has been in doubt since Marineland closed to the public in 2024. Marineland has previously threatened to euthanize the sea mammals, citing a lack of funding to care for them.

In June, the Canadian government signed off on the plan to send the belugas to the American and Spanish aquariums. Earlier this month, U.S. authorities followed suit and signed off on the plan.

Twenty whales — 19 belugas and one killer whale — have died at Marineland since 2019, according to provincial government data obtained through freedom-of-information laws and official statements, the Associated Press reported.

The planned move to the aquariums is controversial, with some animal rights advocates arguing that the belugas are being exported potentially in violation of a 2019 Canadian law that bans the breeding of marine mammals in captivity.

articles.title: Skepticism grows after MAGA-linked farm cleared in parasite outbreak
articles.description: Taylor Farms claimed Monday the FDA apologized for incorrectly linking the California-based farm to a cyclospora parasitic outbreak that sickened over 1,645 people and hospitalized 141. The parasite is known for causing watery or explosive diarrhea, according to Cleveland Clinic . The company had voluntarily recalled Mexican-grown iceberg lettuce Sunday based on FDA guidance, but stated Monday, "Today, we were informed that the FDA made a mistake and this was a false positive." "To be clear, at this moment, FDA has not identified a single positive product test result for Cyclospora," they continued. "Our thoughts remain with everyone who has fallen ill in this outbreak," the company added, "We are committed to working with public health authorities as the ongoing outbreak investigation continues." The Centers for Disease Control is investigating more than 5,100 additional illnesses. The FDA's reversal drew skepticism after Taylor Farms executives reportedly met with White House officials Thursday to distance themselves from the outbreak. Critics questioned the FDA's credibility, with writer Nathan Newman speculating , "Like most people, I assume FDA is lying here to help a big Trump donor And this is horrifying." Health policy analyst Jenn Kaufman warned , "This unfortunately will only further erode confidence in the CDC and public health." Watch the video below. Your browser does not support the video tag.

articles.title: WFP Venezuela Earthquakes Response Situation Report 19 July 2026
articles.description: Country: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) Source: World Food Programme Please refer to the attached file. Situation Update • Twenty-five days after the twin earthquakes of 24 June, authorities report 5,208 deaths and 16,740 injuries. Following search and rescue operations, national authorities have shifted the efforts toward relocating displaced populations to transitional camps. • According to authorities, 107 transitional camps have been established, with 23,828 people currently accommodated. As part of the UN-coordinated response, WFP is supporting three camps with two hot meals daily. • WFP Acting Executive Director Carl Skau spoke with Venezuela's Acting President, Delcy Rodríguez, and reaffirmed the organization's commitment to continuing its support to authorities and humanitarian partners in meeting immediate food needs and assisting affected families in their recovery.

articles.description: KORONADAL CITY — Dredging operations conducted by the Department of Public Works and Highways – Region 12 (DPWH-12) helped protect several towns in Maguindanao del Sur from destructive flooding during the recent onslaught of Super Typhoon Inday and the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat), officials said. The dredging, carried out under the agency’s Oplan Kontra Baha program in partnership with the Maguindanao del Sur provincial government and the Bangsamoro Ministry of Public Works, cleared sections of the Rio Grande de Mindanao and the Buluan River of silt, mud, water hyacinths, and other debris that had been obstructing water flow.
